skill.name: improve-skill
skill.description: Analyze Claude Code, Codex, and Pi session transcripts to improve existing skills or extract new reusable skills.
skill.summary: Extract agent session evidence and turn it into skill improvement or creation workflows.
skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: The shell-execution findings are false positives caused by JavaScript template literals and Markdown backticks. The remaining risk is legitimate filesystem access to hidden agent session and skill directories. Raw transcript reuse also lacks redaction and prompt-injection controls.

remediation.issue: Raw transcripts can carry prompt injection into a fresh agent session.
remediation.suggestion: Treat transcript text as untrusted data, add explicit ignore-instructions guidance, and summarize risky sections before reuse.

remediation.issue: Session transcripts may contain secrets, private code, and tool outputs.
remediation.suggestion: Add a redaction step and warn users before saving transcripts to /tmp or copying them into another agent.

remediation.issue: The workflow accesses hidden agent session and skill directories.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before reading hidden session stores or writing to skill directories.

remediation.issue: Codex session discovery scans recent session files to find a working directory match.
remediation.suggestion: Offer a dry-run listing or require a specific session path when users want a narrower read scope.

semantic_findings.title: Raw Session Transcript Reuse Can Carry Prompt Injection
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells users to paste the extracted transcript into a fresh agent session. Untrusted session text can include instructions that steer the new agent unless isolated and reviewed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited prompt templates embed a session transcript into a new agent workflow with no instruction to treat transcript text as untrusted data. This is a common prompt-injection transfer path.

semantic_findings.description: The script reads local agent session files and prints message content. The documentation also suggests saving the transcript in /tmp, which may expose secrets or private project data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script reads the selected session file and prints the formatted transcript, while the documentation redirects output to a temporary file. I found no redaction or secret scanning step in the cited workflow.

content.value_statement: Skill authors need clear evidence from real agent sessions. This skill extracts transcripts and turns them into prompts for improving or creating skills.
actual_capabilities: Extracts recent Claude Code, Pi, or Codex session transcripts for the current working directory.
Parses JSONL session records into a readable role-based transcript.
Supports selecting an agent, custom working directory, or explicit session file.
Builds workflows for improving an existing skill from transcript evidence.
Provides a creation workflow for turning a session into a new skill.
limitations: Reads local session history and may expose sensitive prompts, code, or tool outputs.
Does not redact secrets or classify sensitive content before output.
Requires users to copy generated prompts into a separate agent session.
Handles only supported session formats and recent Codex sessions matching the working directory.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Review a real agent session and identify missing instructions, examples, and corrections for a current skill.

use_cases.title: Create a Reusable Skill
use_cases.description: Turn a successful coding session into a reusable workflow that other agents can follow.

use_cases.title: Document Agent Workflow Lessons
use_cases.description: Extract repeated failures, workarounds, and successful patterns from session history for team review.

prompt_templates.title: Find Skill Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of the latest session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use improve-skill to extract my current session and list the top missing instructions in the skill I used.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Improvement Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a fresh session for skill editing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the latest Claude Code session for this project and draft a concise improvement prompt for the existing skill.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Specific Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a chosen transcript instead of auto-detection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this specific Codex session file to identify examples, corrections, and warnings that should be added to my skill.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Safe Skill Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review with security and quality constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the transcript against the current skill and produce a prioritized edit plan with redaction notes and risk checks.

output_examples.input: Improve the deployment skill using my latest Codex session.
output_examples.output: A readable transcript summary, a list of skill gaps, and a prompt for a fresh session to update the skill.

output_examples.input: Create a new skill from a successful debugging session.
output_examples.output: A proposed skill focus, key workflow steps, common pitfalls, and example usage guidance.

output_examples.input: Review a session where the agent kept retrying commands.
output_examples.output: A focused analysis of confusion points, missing examples, and clearer instructions for future agents.

best_practices: Review transcripts for secrets before sharing them with another agent.
Use explicit skill paths and confirm the target skill before editing.
Keep improvement prompts focused on observed failures and successful patterns.
anti_patterns: Do not paste raw production secrets or private customer data into new sessions.
Do not run transcript extraction from shared machines without consent.
Do not treat generated improvement prompts as reviewed skill changes.

faq.question: What session formats does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude Code, Pi, and Codex JSONL session files documented by the skill.

faq.question: Does it edit skills automatically?
faq.answer: No. It helps generate prompts and workflows that guide a separate skill editing session.

faq.question: Can it use a specific session file?
faq.answer: Yes. The extractor accepts an explicit session path when auto-detection is not enough.

faq.question: Does it redact sensitive data?
faq.answer: No. Users should review and redact transcripts before copying them into another agent session.

faq.question: Why does it use a fresh session?
faq.answer: A fresh session keeps the improvement task focused on the transcript and the target skill.

faq.question: Is it safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Session transcripts may contain private code, paths, commands, and tool outputs.
